meta.title: Jon, here is what I believe we are called to carry, and where I need your help
meta.subtitle: This is not a pitch. It is me trying to write down, honestly, what the Lord has put in front of us, what is already happening, what I am carrying, and the decisions I cannot make well on my own.
meta.confidentialNote: Private working notes between Ryan Fox and Jon Perron. Please do not forward the page or the access code.

sections.heading: What I believe the Lord has called us to
sections.lede: Before any of the systems or the money, this is the part I want you to hear clearly. Everything else on this page is downstream of it.

blocks.text: The table is the ministry. Making disciples who make disciples, in homes and at kitchen tables and in ordinary weeks, with people whose names we know. The systems and the organization exist to support that and to help it multiply. They are not the point.
Here is how I understand the pieces fitting together right now.

items: USA Missionaries is the covering. It recruits, equips, supports, and connects missionaries across the United States, and it holds the 501(c)(3), the giving, and the accountability.
Kitchen Table Gospel is the ministry itself. It is what happens at the table and through everyday relationships: homes, groups, coffee shops, a couple sitting with another couple.
Discipleship Operating System helps those relationships continue, get supported, and multiply. It helps me remember, follow up, and see where fruit is actually forming.
Mission of Reconciliation helps people walk in freedom, reconciliation, purpose, and service.
Fourth Quarter is an emerging pathway for recruiting mature believers to disciple the next generation.

blocks.text: I want to say more about Mission of Reconciliation, because it is easy to file it as a freedom ministry and stop there. It is more than that. Freedom is where it starts, but the deeper work is helping people walk in reconciliation: with God, with the people they have hurt or been hurt by, and with the purpose they have been avoiding. And a large part of who we are meant to reach is not the young. It is seasoned believers in the fourth quarter of their lives who have been sidelined, or who sidelined themselves, and who are carrying decades of walking with God that nobody is asking them for.

blocks.title: Fourth Quarter
blocks.text: That is the idea I am calling Fourth Quarter. Recruit mature believers, people in the last quarter of life, into purposeful service, and specifically into discipling the next generation. It is still forming. One of the questions further down is whether it should become a real pathway inside DOS or stay a conviction I carry informally for now.
The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. I do not think our problem has ever been the harvest. It has been workers who know how to reproduce.
blocks.attribution: What I keep coming back to

sections.heading: What is already happening
sections.lede: I want you to see that this is no longer just vision. Real relationships, referrals, groups, giving, and the beginnings of multiplication are already here.

blocks.text: At the table, week to week: two men's groups, individual discipleship relationships, and couples and individuals arriving through referrals faster than I expected. Several couples in different states are in conversations about apprenticing beside Brooke and me. I will name them further down.

items.label: Meetings logged
items.note: Verified from DOS over the most recent reporting period. Real, not illustrative.

items.label: Hours invested
items.note: Same period, same source. Time actually spent sitting with people.

blocks.note: These two are the only real activity figures on this page. Every organization wide number you will see in the dashboard examples is invented for illustration.

blocks.text: The fruit I am most encouraged by is Tanner, who is moving from being discipled toward discipling others. That is the whole thing, in one person. Resources, journeys, prayer, and follow up are all live in DOS with real ministry data, and there are stories and testimonies ready to share.

Underneath it, the foundation is real too: the 501(c)(3), the missionary application, giving and finance and documents and onboarding running in Operations, and the communications platform and newsletter close to release.

sections.heading: What I am carrying right now
sections.lede: This is the section I would most like to skip, which is probably why it belongs here. I need you to see the whole load, not the parts that look good.

blocks.text: First, the things that come before any of the ministry: my quiet time, my marriage, and our five children. Brooke homeschools all five, runs the household, and helps me with the ministry on top of it. Any plan that quietly assumes more of her is not a plan.

Then the ministry itself. Two long weekly men's groups, Tuesday morning and Wednesday evening. Individual discipleship. Couples ministry. Referrals that keep increasing. Training couples at the table.
Then the organization. Fundraising. Product direction and review for DOS. Operations. Partnerships. The newsletter. And everything under finance: donor stewardship, accounting, legal, and compliance.

blocks.title: Brooke and SHINE
blocks.text: Brooke is contracting with SHINE to coordinate one event, SHINE Founders Weekend, October 1 through October 4, 2026. It could lead to more work with them later, but nothing beyond that one event is committed, and I do not want to describe it as though it were. Her goal is to do this one well, document it, and hand it off cleanly.

blocks.title: What I cannot keep doing
blocks.text: I cannot sustain the current pace alone, and I know it. What I uniquely bring is the spiritual vision, the frontline relationships, the training, the product direction, and the fundraising. Routine execution keeps landing on me anyway. We need development capacity, and we need redundancy, so that the ministry does not depend on one person staying upright.

sections.heading: What I can see DOS becoming
sections.lede: Right now DOS helps me remember what is happening with the people I disciple. I think it can do considerably more than that, and I would rather show you than describe it.

blocks.text: I can see DOS becoming more than a tool for one discipler. It could help a church or a ministry see where discipleship is actually happening, where people are following through, where multiplication is starting, and where someone may need attention before they quietly drop off.

The part I care most about is that the individual experience stays simple. The person being discipled should never feel like they are inside a reporting system. Leadership sees the fruit in aggregate. Nobody's private conversation gets exposed to make that possible.

I had two concept views built, one for a multi campus church and one for a ministry working with service members and veterans across regions. Both are mockups with invented numbers. Neither organization has seen them, and neither has agreed to anything. They are here so you can picture what a tailored view of DOS could become.

blocks.note: Both are illustrative concepts. The figures are invented. Neither is a live account, a current integration, or an existing partnership.

sections.heading: Who we are praying through, training, and considering
sections.lede: The model that seems to work is apprenticeship: a couple serves beside Brooke and me at the table, grows into leading, and eventually helps train others. These are the people in that process right now.

blocks.text: I want to be careful here. These are people we are praying through, training, vetting, or simply considering. It is not a roster and nobody on it has signed anything. The status column is the honest one.

blocks.caption: People we are praying through and training, not finished commitments. The last column is what keeps me from hearing interest and filing it as a yes.

sections.heading: What we are exploring
sections.lede: These are real conversations and real ideas, and some of them are good. None of them is an established commitment, and I do not want to talk about them as if they were.

blocks.title: Read this first
blocks.text: Everything in this section is being evaluated. Some are conversations that have happened. Some are ideas I keep returning to. If I had to guess, most will not happen, or will not happen soon. I am listing them so you can see what is pulling on my attention, not so you can count them as commitments.

items: ZOE Church marriage ministry. A possible church partnership built around training couples through apprenticeship at the table. Scope, leaders, curriculum, timing, and who owns it would all need to be clear before anything launched.
Engage Your Destiny. A ministry to service members and veterans where a tailored DOS view might genuinely help. Nothing agreed. The concept page above is my imagination, not their request.
SAVE Standard. Related to our work but separate from it. My role, the organizational boundary, and a time limit would need defining so it does not blur into the core calling.
The Lord's Army. Same category as SAVE Standard: related, separate, and needing a clear home before I give it more than conversation.
Tent Maiker. The biggest of these. I describe it below.
Other church and para ministry partnerships, including organizations like Mac Ministries that could use a customized DOS experience.
Whether Fourth Quarter becomes a formal pathway within DOS, or stays a conviction I carry informally for now.

blocks.title: Tent Maiker
blocks.text: Tent Maiker is a possible AI development company. The idea is that it could help contractors, businesses, churches, and ministries build systems and capacity without each of them hiring a full internal team, while creating revenue that helps fund Kingdom work and a development team of our own. Chicken Coop Company and Come to Life Concrete are viable first pilots. If the initial model works, other contractors and ministry partners could follow. Possible, not decided, and one of the questions below is whether it is a real path or a distraction.

I am trying to be careful with the word partnership. A conversation is not a partnership. A pilot is not a partnership. Please push back where you think I am holding one of these more tightly than I should.

sections.heading: Where the money actually is, and what needs to move off me
sections.lede: Two things here. The financial picture, stated exactly, and the responsibilities that cannot keep converging on one person.

blocks.text: These figures get confused with each other constantly, so I want to say plainly what each one is and is not.

items.label: Cumulative giving
items.note: Everything given since we started, across 43 Planning Center records synced August 20, 2026. This is a total over time. It is not money we have.

items.label: Current bank balance
items.note: What is actually in the account, reported September 20, 2026. This is the cash figure.

items.label: Monthly support
items.note: Committed recurring monthly support. The public profile shows this as 41% funded.

items.label: Monthly goal
items.note: What full monthly support would look like.

items.label: Monthly gap
items.note: The difference between committed monthly support and the goal. If one number stays with you, make it this one.

blocks.note: Cumulative giving is not cash on hand, and monthly support is not either. I am deliberately not stating a runway, because I have not yet verified monthly operating expenses and household obligations, and a runway figure built on guesses would be worse than none.

blocks.text: The opportunity is real. So is the limit. What I uniquely need to lead is the spiritual direction, the frontline relationships, the training, product direction, fundraising, and partner development. Almost everything else should be able to move to someone else eventually, and right now most of it has not.
Those are the four seats I think need sizing and sequencing. I am not asking to fill all of them. I am asking which one comes first, and what we can responsibly afford given the numbers above.

sections.heading: What I need Jon's help discerning
sections.lede: You have been generous with your time already. These are the things I genuinely cannot see clearly from the inside.

items.prompt: What is the primary assignment for the next 90 days?
items.detail: If I could only protect one thing, what should it be?

items.prompt: What should I explicitly pause, decline, or defer?
items.detail: I am better at adding than subtracting. I would like your read on what to close, out loud.

items.prompt: What weekly ceiling protects my spiritual health, my marriage, our family, and the frontline ministry?
items.detail: A number, if you have one. I will hold to it better if it comes from you.

items.prompt: What is the first responsibility or role that must move off me?
items.detail: Of the four seats above, which one first, and what can we afford?

items.prompt: Should Tent Maiker help fund development capacity, and under what safeguards?
items.detail: It is the one idea that could change the funding picture. It is also the one that could quietly consume a year.

items.prompt: What short scorecard should you and I review each week?
items.detail: We have already settled on meeting weekly. What I do not know is which handful of numbers we should look at every time, so the meeting stays useful instead of drifting.

blocks.title: Our rhythm is already decided
blocks.text: We meet weekly: in person every other week, and by phone or Google Meet on the alternating weeks. Question six is about what we look at when we meet, not whether we meet.
